# All-status anchored residual credit and an arbitrary-shape thirteen-volume payment

The first theorem extends the archived small-cap-budget residual-root
depletion lemma to every capture status by explicitly pricing a full
source-fiber capture. It allows arbitrary anchored barycentric relations,
not only reflected pairs. It gives necessary numerical inequalities at
a hypothetical bad family; it does not assert that enough paying anchored
relations exist there. The last section proves that the particular
thirteen-volume strict-quota certificate is safe for EVERY compatible
choice of positive convex fiber shapes, in every d>=1.

## 1. Actual fibers, cap volumes, and the credit

Let C be a convex body in R^n x R^d, d>=1, with positive d-volume fibers
K_z at a finite set P of integer bases. Write V_z=|K_z|. Fix p in P and
distinct other bases z_1,...,z_m with strictly positive coefficients
lambda_j summing to one and

    p=sum_j lambda_j z_j.

Set v_j=V_(z_j)^(1/d). For h>=0 define

    Delta(h)=(sum_j lambda_j v_j - h^(1/d))_+,

    R_lambda(h)=min_j {
       V_(z_j) - (v_j-Delta(h)/lambda_j)_+^d }.       (1)

Here t_+=max(t,0). In particular 0<=R_lambda(h)<=min_j V_(z_j),
and R_lambda is continuous and nonincreasing in h.

**Theorem.** For every closed ambient halfspace H, let

    h=|K_p intersect H_p^c|,
    U_j=|K_(z_j) intersect H_(z_j)|.

Then

    sum_j U_j >= R_lambda(h).                        (2)

All normals are allowed. In particular no separate orientation,
proper-cut, or nonzero-continuous-normal premise is needed.

## 2. Proof including full and empty residuals

Put B=sum_j U_j and V_min=min_j V_(z_j). If B>=V_min, equation (2)
follows from R_lambda<=V_min. This covers every case in which one source
fiber is captured in full. The proof below is not applied to a zero
volume residual.

Suppose B<V_min. Every source residual has positive d-volume. Their
weighted Minkowski combination belongs to the residual fiber at p:
the base coordinates average to p, convexity puts the combined point in
C, and the strict complementary halfspace inequality is preserved under
a positive weighted average. Brunn--Minkowski therefore gives

    h^(1/d) >= sum_j lambda_j (V_(z_j)-U_j)^(1/d).    (3)

The open residuals have the same volume as their convex closures. One
may apply the usual compact-body form to their closures, whose weighted
sum lies in the closure of the source residual. When the continuous
normal is nonzero the separating plane has zero d-volume. When it is
zero, each residual is either a whole fiber or empty; in the present
positive-residual branch the strict affine base inequalities themselves
imply that the whole source fiber is residual. Thus (3) is also valid
in that case. If h=0, (3) contradicts positivity, which simply excludes
this branch.

If Delta(h)=0 there is nothing to prove. Otherwise use the nonnegative,
increasing convex functions

    f_j(s)=lambda_j[v_j-(V_(z_j)-s)^(1/d)],
                        0<=s<=B<V_min.

For B=0, (3) already forces Delta=0. For B>0, convexity and f_j(0)=0 give

    Delta(h) <= sum_j f_j(U_j)
               <=sum_j (U_j/B)f_j(B)
               <=max_j f_j(B).                       (4)

Choose j attaining the last maximum. Since B<V_(z_j), the bound
Delta<=f_j(B) also implies Delta<lambda_j v_j. Inverting this one
inequality gives

    B >= V_(z_j)-(v_j-Delta/lambda_j)^d
      >=R_lambda(h).

This completes (2). For d=1 the convex functions in (4) are linear, so
the same proof applies without a limiting interpretation.

The scalar escape at V_min is indispensable: once one entire source
fiber is captured, its empty residual cannot be inserted into (3).
The new statement resolves that status exactly instead of silently
continuing positive-volume Brunn--Minkowski through an empty set.

At the level of these scalar alternatives the inverse formula is exact.
If 0<R_lambda(h)<V_min, spend exactly R_lambda(h) on a minimizing
index and zero on the others; the residual-root inequality is equality.
If R_lambda(h)=V_min, a full smallest-fiber capture invokes the escape
alternative. These are scalar extremizers of the stated information,
not claims that every allocation is geometrically realizable in fixed
bodies.

## 3. One deterministic center and several anchored relations

Let y in K_p have ordinary raw depth at least delta>0. For any halfspace
containing Y=(p,y), its own-fiber capture q is at least delta; hence
h=V_p-q<=V_p-delta. Applying (2) gives

    mixed raw depth at Y
      >=delta+R_lambda(V_p-delta).                   (5)

This point is one actual point of S. The inequalities hold for every
closed ambient halfspace, including those with purely integer normals.

For a finite collection E of anchored relations at the same p, let J_e
be the set of source bases of relation e, with p excluded. Choose numbers
theta_e>=0 such that

    sum_(e:z in J_e) theta_e <=1 for every z!=p.

Multiplying (2) by theta_e and summing counts every actual captured
fiber volume at most once. Therefore

    D_raw(p,y) >=delta+
        sum_e theta_e R_e(V_p-delta).                (6)

The maximum over these theta exists: this is a closed finite polytope,
and each theta_e<=1 because its source set is nonempty. Thus (6) provides
a finite, attained sufficient mass allocation at ONE actual anchor.
It does not assert that its value meets OC for arbitrary data.

Taking y=g_(K_p), delta=Gamma_d V_p supplies an unconditional center
choice. If a particular anchored relation has exact BM root equality
sum lambda_j v_j=V_p^(1/d), its credit is explicitly (1) with

    Delta=V_p^(1/d)[1-(1-Gamma_d)^(1/d)].             (7)

Consequently any hypothetical bad family with maximum raw depth less
than Gamma_d M/k must, at EVERY p, satisfy

    Gamma_d V_p + max_theta sum_e theta_e
        R_e((1-Gamma_d)V_p) < Gamma_d M/k.           (8)

This is a necessary actual-geometric inequality, including all full-cut
escape cases. Neither (7) nor (8) proves that a minimizer has enough tight
anchored inclusions to violate it. The all-midpoint-tight theorem and
its forest counterexamples remain separate.

## 4. Every shape with the thirteen certified volumes is safe

Use the thirteen-point complete lattice base P and its volume vector w
from `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
Their total is one and occupied parity count is seven. Consider ANY
actual compatible positive convex d-fibers with these volumes, d>=1.
There is no box, symmetry, centroid-affinity, or equality assumption.

The actual integer relation is

    p_7=(1,0,1)=(p_12+p_1+p_9)/3,
    p_12=(2,0,1), p_1=(0,-2,0), p_9=(1,2,2).

Write

    v=w_7=58/455,
    (b_1,b_2,b_3)=(w_12,w_1,w_9)
                  =(58/455,1179/14560,13/168).

Choose the actual point Y=(p_7,g_(K_(p_7))). I claim that EVERY closed
ambient halfspace containing Y captures more than 1/100 total mass in
these three other fibers. Suppose otherwise. Each of their captures is
then at most 1/100, and their residual volumes are positive and at least
b_j-1/100. The residual source volume is at most (1-Gamma_d)v.
Equation (3) and arithmetic-geometric mean would imply

    ((1-Gamma_d)v)^(1/d)
       >=(1/3)sum_j (b_j-1/100)^(1/d)
       >=[product_j(b_j-1/100)]^(1/(3d)).             (9)

But exact rational arithmetic gives

    product_j(b_j-1/100)-(7v/11)^3
        =1348713982727/48144144048000000 >0.         (10)

Also Gamma_d>4/11 for every d>=1. For an elementary verification,
(1+1/d)^d is smaller than sum_(j>=0)1/j!, and the latter is at most
8/3+5/96=87/32<11/4: the tail beginning at j=4 is bounded by the
geometric series (1/24)sum_(r>=0)(1/5)^r=5/96.
Thus (10) makes the right-hand side of (9) strictly larger than its
left-hand side, a contradiction. Purely integer cuts are already
included in the residual argument of Section 2.

The own-fiber capture is at least Gamma_d v. The infimum over all caps
therefore satisfies the uniform bound

    D_raw(Y) >=Gamma_d(58/455)+1/100
              =Gamma_d/7 +1/100-Gamma_d/65
              >=Gamma_d/7+3/1300.                  (11)

The last inequality uses Gamma_d<=1/2, which follows from
(1+1/d)^d>=2. Pointwise strictness of the three-fiber payment is not
mistaken for strictness of an infimum: the FIXED surplus 3/1300 in (11)
establishes the asserted strict margin uniformly.

Since the total original mass is one, (11) is also normalized depth.
It proves the occupied-parity bound, and hence OC with n=3, for every
compatible family with this volume vector. This does not invalidate the
strict-quota certificate: that certificate proves only that all mass
quotas can coexist with compatibility. The new conclusion uses actual
residual caps at a common barycentric anchor, information absent from
those quotas. It does not show that every admissible quota vector has a
paying relation, or that a bad minimizer must acquire one.
